text.tspan: AWS Global Accelerator: enter the AWS network at the nearest edge, via anycast IPs
Without: public internet all the way
Every ISP hop adds latency, jitter and packet loss.
Client caches the DNS answer: after a failover it can
keep using a dead IP until the TTL ends.
one server holds one IP address
ALL servers hold the SAME IP address and the
client is routed to the NEAREST one
Global Accelerator announces its static IPs
from many AWS edge locations at once.
• Uses the AWS internal network to reach your app: 2 anycast IPs are created → traffic goes to the nearest edge location → the edge sends it to your app.
• The edge terminates the client's TCP connection and opens a new one to your endpoint almost at once (faster handshakes).
• The IPs stay the same for the life of the accelerator (even if disabled); you lose them only when you delete it. DNS name: xxxx.awsglobalaccelerator.com.
• The two IPv4 addresses come from two separate network zones (if one zone fails, the other IP still works).
• AWS: up to 60% better performance for TCP and UDP traffic (FAQ). Pricing: fixed hourly fee per accelerator + Data Transfer-Premium per GB.
